title: Closed immersion on small etale sheaves of sets
statement: Let $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ be a closed immersion of schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-closed-immersion] and $j:U=X\setminus i(Z)\hookrightarrow X$ its complementary open immersion [def-weil-open-immersion]. On the small etale topoi [def-weil-pbc-etale-site], the direct image $i_*:\operatorname{Sh}(Z_{\mathrm{Et}})\to\operatorname{Sh}(X_{\mathrm{Et}})$ on sheaves of sets [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaf-of-sets] is fully faithful, and its essential image consists exactly of the sheaves $F$ whose restriction $j^{-1}F$ is the terminal sheaf on $U_{\mathrm{Et}}$. The counit $i^{-1}i_*\to\operatorname{id}$ is an isomorphism. Here inverse and direct image are the geometric-morphism adjoints [def-trf-geometric-morphism], concretely the set-sheaf adjunction of [lem-weil-pbc-sets-etale-inverse-image-composition-units].

source.place: Tag 04CA, proposition-closed-immersion-pushforward, part (1) and final assertion (sheaves of sets, not only abelian sheaves).

proof.text: Work with sheaves of sets and the small representatives fixed by [def-weil-size-convention]. Write $L=i^{-1}$, $R=i_*$, and $\eta,\varepsilon$ for their adjunction unit and counit. The set-valued construction of [lem-weil-pbc-sets-etale-inverse-image-composition-units] gives $(RG)(V)=G(V\times_X Z)$ and defines $i^*a$ as the image of a section $a$ under $\eta$. We use this construction for $i$ and $j$. The adjunction in [def-trf-geometric-morphism] supplies naturality and the triangle identities. The empty open subscheme is an etale object by [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-etale]. The empty family covers it, so the equalizer sheaf condition in [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaf-of-sets] says $G(\varnothing)$ is a singleton. These constructions and equalities hold also for empty schemes.

source.place: Tag 04CA, proposition-closed-immersion-pushforward, setup; empty-cover observation in the proof of Tag 04FX, lemma-stalk-pushforward-closed-immersion

proof.text:
Fix a geometric point $\bar z$ of $Z$ and put $\bar x=i\bar z$. The initiality assertion of [lemma-openclosed-stalk-lowerstar] concerns the categories of pointed etale neighbourhoods, independently of coefficients: $\Phi:\mathrm N(\bar x)\to\mathrm N(\bar z)$ sends $V$ to $V_Z$. The stalk definition and step 1 give a canonical comparison
$$r_{G,\bar z}:(RG)_{\bar x}=\operatorname{colim}_{\mathrm N(\bar x)^{op}}G(V_Z)\longrightarrow G_{\bar z}.$$
Here is why the existing initiality assertion gives a bijection for sets, without using an abelian-coefficient theorem. For every set $A$, apply [lem-weil-pbc-initial-functor-limit] to $\Phi$ and the covariant diagram $W\mapsto\operatorname{Hom}(G(W),A)$ on $\mathrm N(\bar z)$. By the colimit universal property [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit], its limit is $\operatorname{Hom}(G_{\bar z},A)$, and its restricted limit is $\operatorname{Hom}((RG)_{\bar x},A)$. Thus precomposition with $r_{G,\bar z}$ is bijective for every $A$. Taking $A$ to be its source gives a left inverse; injectivity for $A$ its target shows this inverse is also a right inverse. The map $r$ sends the germ of $b\in G(V_Z)$ at $(V,\bar v)$ to the germ of the same $b$ at $(V_Z,(\bar v,\bar z))$; it is natural in $G$.

source.place: Tag 04FX, lemma-stalk-pushforward-closed-immersion, on-Z calculation; the coefficient-independent initiality is supplied by lemma-openclosed-stalk-lowerstar, and the limit theorem is Categories Tag 002R

proof.text: For a set sheaf $G$ on $Z$, let $c=c_{i,\bar z,RG}:(LRG)_{\bar z}\xrightarrow{\sim}(RG)_{\bar x}$ be the bijection of [lem-weil-pbc-sets-etale-inverse-image-stalk-germ]. We claim that the stalk of the actual counit $\varepsilon_G:LRG\to G$ is $r_{G,\bar z}\circ c$. Indeed, take $b\in(RG)(V)=G(V_Z)$. The right triangle identity $R\varepsilon_G\circ\eta_{RG}=1_{RG}$, evaluated at $V$, says that $\varepsilon_G$ sends $i^*b\in(LRG)(V_Z)$ to $b$. On germs this agrees with $r\circ c$, by the germ formulas for $c$ and step 2. These germs exhaust $(LRG)_{\bar z}$: their images under the bijection $c$ are every represented germ of $(RG)_{\bar x}$. Therefore $(\varepsilon_G)_{\bar z}$ is bijective. Applying [lem-weil-pbc-sets-etale-iso-on-geometric-stalks] on $Z$ shows that every $\varepsilon_G$ is an isomorphism. The counit is consequently a natural isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 04CA, proposition-closed-immersion-pushforward, first sentence of proof; Tag 03Q1, lemma-stalk-pullback (3), for the germ-compatible inverse-image comparison

proof.text: The counit isomorphisms of step 3 make $R$ fully faithful. Explicitly, the adjunction sends a morphism $\alpha:RG\to RH$ to $\varepsilon_H\circ L\alpha:LRG\to H$. Precomposing with $\varepsilon_G^{-1}:G\to LRG$ gives a bijection $\operatorname{Hom}(RG,RH)\to\operatorname{Hom}(G,H)$. Its inverse is $\beta\mapsto R\beta$, since naturality gives $\varepsilon_H\circ LR\beta=\beta\circ\varepsilon_G$. This proves both fullness and faithfulness and retains the specified counit, rather than only an unspecified left-inverse isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 04CA, proposition-closed-immersion-pushforward, formal full-faithfulness inference in proof

proof.text: The open immersion $j$ is an etale object by [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-etale]. For a geometric point $\bar x$ in $U$, any pointed etale neighbourhood $(V,\bar v)$ can be restricted to $(V\times_XU,(\bar v,\bar x))$; this is again a pointed etale neighbourhood, by the fibre products in [def-weil-pbc-etale-site]. It is disjoint from $Z$. Thus every germ of $RG$ restricts to the unique element of $G(\varnothing)$, and any two such germs agree on the common pointed refinement $(V_1\times_XV_2)\times_XU$. The neighbourhood $U$ itself supplies that element, so $(RG)_{\bar x}$ is a singleton, by the stalk colimit [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks] and step 1. The germ-compatible inverse-image comparison [lem-weil-pbc-sets-etale-inverse-image-stalk-germ], applied to $j$, now shows that every geometric stalk of $j^{-1}RG$ is a singleton. The terminal sheaf $1$ assigns a singleton to every object; its stalk is a singleton as well. The unique map $j^{-1}RG\to1$ is an isomorphism by [lem-weil-pbc-sets-etale-iso-on-geometric-stalks] on $U$. Hence every sheaf in the essential image has terminal open restriction.

source.place: Tag 04FX, lemma-stalk-pushforward-closed-immersion, off-Z paragraph; Tag 04CA, proposition-closed-immersion-pushforward, essential-image inclusion

proof.text:
Conversely let $F$ be a set sheaf with $j^{-1}F\cong1$, and consider its actual unit $\eta_F:F\to RLF$. At $\bar x=i\bar z$, compose its stalk map with the bijections from step 2 and the inverse-image germ comparison:
$$F_{\bar x}\xrightarrow{(\eta_F)_{\bar x}}(RLF)_{\bar x}\xrightarrow{r_{LF,\bar z}}(LF)_{\bar z}\xrightarrow{c_{i,\bar z,F}}F_{\bar x}.$$
A germ represented by $a\in F(V)$ is sent first to the germ of $i^*a$ viewed as a section of $RLF$ at $V$, then to its germ at $V_Z$, and finally back to the germ of $a$. This is precisely the unit-section formula of [lem-weil-pbc-sets-etale-inverse-image-composition-units] and the germ formula of [lem-weil-pbc-sets-etale-inverse-image-stalk-germ]. The composite is the identity, so $(\eta_F)_{\bar x}$ is bijective. At a point in $U$, the source stalk is a singleton by the same inverse-image comparison for $j$ and the assumption on $j^{-1}F$; the target stalk is a singleton by step 5 applied to $G=LF$. Every geometric point of $X$ is of one of these two kinds: in the closed image it factors uniquely through $Z$, since locally $Z=\operatorname{Spec}(B/I)$ and the field-valued map kills $I$ [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Stalk detection [lem-weil-pbc-sets-etale-iso-on-geometric-stalks] gives $\eta_F$ an isomorphism. Therefore $F\cong i_*(i^{-1}F)$ lies in the essential image, as required.

source.place: Tag 04CA, proposition-closed-immersion-pushforward, converse essential-image argument using the unit; Tag 03Q1, lemma-stalk-pullback (3)

split_report.summary: Proved the sets version of Stacks 04CA in six steps with no new nodes. Reused only the coefficient-independent initiality clause of the existing closed-pushforward stalk node, converting it to a set-valued comparison by the existing initial-functor limit theorem and the colimit universal property. Verified the actual counit and actual essential-image unit on represented germs, and terminal restriction by the empty-cover and off-closed-image stalk calculation. The abelian-only full-faithfulness and essential-image results are not used. Added explicit references for set sheaves and the set-valued adjunction; mathematical statement unchanged.

The inherited ancestry through lem-trf-oriented-source-localization is preserved; no chapter or unit route is changed.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-NI-0c6c446fe (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: Read in full: the item, all six steps, and the statement of every cited node; there are no new nodes. Statement: matches Stacks Tag 04CA (etale-cohomology.tex, proposition-closed-immersion-pushforward), part (1) and its final left-inverse sentence, for sheaves of sets. No hypothesis is added or dropped and nothing is weakened. Step 1: G(empty) is a singleton because the empty family covers the empty open (open-immersion leaf). Step 2: uses only the initiality clause of lemma-openclosed-stalk-lowerstar, turned into a bijection of set-valued stalks through the Hom(G(W),A) limit (initial-functor-limit leaf plus the colimit universal property). This is the same argument as the blueprint's prop-openclosed-lowerstar-fully-faithful proof. Step 3: the triangle identity gives eps(i^*b)=b, so the counit stalk equals r composed with c, and stalk detection on Z finishes. Step 4: standard adjunction algebra. Step 5: neighbourhoods refined by V x_X U miss Z, so stalks over U are singletons. Step 6: c composed with r composed with the unit is the identity on germs; stalks over U are singletons on both sides; the closed-immersion affine clause gives the dichotomy of geometric points. Edge cases checked: X, Z or U empty, non-reduced Z, empty stalks on Z. Duplicates: lem-kun-04ca is the abelian version, prop-openclosed-lowerstar-fully-faithful is the counit clause only, and no set-valued 04CA node exists. Accepted tool_uses: lemma-openclosed-stalk-lowerstar and the two set-sheaf inverse-image nodes, all Lean-closed generic tools. No SGA source. No fixes made.

lean.statement: theorem etaleClosedComplementSets {X Z : Scheme.{u}} (i : Z ⟶ X) [IsClosedImmersion i] : (etaleSetDirectImage i).Full ∧ (etaleSetDirectImage i).Faithful ∧ (∀ F : Sheaf X.smallEtaleTopology (Type (u + 1)), (etaleSetDirectImage i).essImage F ↔ Nonempty (IsTerminal ((etaleSetInverseImage (i.openComplement.ι)).obj F))) ∧ (∀ G : Sheaf Z.smallEtaleTopology (Type (u + 1)), IsIso ((etaleSetAdjunction i).counit.app G))
